title: kernel timeline bucketization and span alignment for runtime perf traces
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem:
We currently emit NVTX ranges and spans from multiple runtime components (prefill scheduler, decode scheduler, kernel launch helpers) but the resulting traces are noisy and hard to aggregate for per-kernel attribution at scale. Kernel names vary across builds and quantization variants; tight per-call spans create O(10-20%) overhead when sampling at high rates.

Goal:
Produce a stable, low-overhead runtime telemetry surface that lets SREs and perf engineers: (1) attribute latency and GPU time to kernel families and variants, (2) view end-to-end prefill->decode timelines with correct causal span alignment across devices/streams, and (3) slice by sequence length buckets and batching characteristics.

Approach overview:
- Introduce server-side kernel timeline bucketization: collapse high-frequency kernel invocations into coalesced NVTX buckets keyed by kernel fingerprint + variant tag, aggregated per-request.
- Attach a lightweight span_id and causal tags at prefill enqueue, carry through scheduler and kernel launcher, and close spans at bucket boundaries rather than for each kernel launch.
- Add sequence-length/seq-bucket tags and batch-size tags to spans to enable percentile-based breakdowns in Grafana.
- Update trace exporter to emit per-bucket summaries (count, cumulative GPU time, max latency) and occasional sampled per-kernel raw spans (1/5000 by default) for debugging.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Granularity vs overhead: coalesced buckets reduce overhead at expense of per-kernel exactness. We intentionally keep raw per-kernel sampling rare and targeted to problematic kernels.
- Fingerprinting approach: we will use a stable kernel signature derived from (op_name, major_version, quant_type, tile_shape) rather than raw symbol names to avoid noise across builds. This requires a short mapping table maintained in code.
- Cross-device correlation: enforce a monotonic request-level UUID that is propagated through RPCs; this increases payload by ~16 bytes but is necessary for causal stitching.

Acceptance criteria:
- New telemetry emits bucketized NVTX ranges for 100% of requests in canary cluster with <2% added p50 latency.
- Grafana dashboard shows breakdown by kernel_fingerprint and seq_bucket with <30s ingestion latency in our dev stack.
- E2E correlation validated: a traced request shows contiguous spans from prefill enqueue -> scheduler -> kernel_bucket -> decode finalization in at least 95% of sampled traces.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag on by default in dev/staging. 2) Canary on 1% of production traffic for 48 hours, monitor overhead & correctness. 3) Gradual ramp to 25% -> 100% if no regressions.

Notes on backwards compatibility:
- Traces from older runtime versions without bucketization will still be accepted by the backend; dashboard will display an "unbucketed" lane.

Measurement plan:
- Create a Grafana panel comparing kernel-attributed GPU-time before/after for the same workload.
- SLI: percent of traces with end-to-end stitching; SLO guardrail: <5% increase in 95th latency from tracing instrumentation.
